  - region "Simple English explanation of Horizontal Stretch and Compression":
    - paragraph: In simple English
    - heading "Understand Horizontal Stretch and Compression" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "A horizontal scale uses the reciprocal of the inside factor. f(2x) compresses width by 1/2: the old x=2 output of x^2 appears at x=1. f(x/2) stretches by 2. A useful rule is Horizontal scale: g(x)=f(cx). You can learn Horizontal Stretch and Compression by trying one small example instead of long theory."
    - paragraph: "Take the reciprocal of the inside multiplier to read the new width, then check one key point. Example: What does f(2x) do? The inside factor is 2. Use reciprocal width 1/2. So the answer is horizontal compression."
    - paragraph: "In real life, video speed: Faster playback compresses time. Watch out: Saying f(2x) stretches by 2. Horizontal scale uses the reciprocal."
    - complementary:
      - generic: Try this example
      - paragraph: What does f(2x) do?
      - generic "Compare your answer"
